pure-announcement.rationale: Official, evergreen documentation of a long-standing security architecture (publisher trust since v1.97, marketplace scanning long predating that), not a launch or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: extension-registry-trust argues closed curation is the only defensible posture given no sandbox and explicitly calls scale/reputation/takedown remedies 'the wrong timing'; this note is the concrete operational counter-example — a real, major marketplace that chose open submission plus a specific layered-scanning-and-monitoring stack instead, with mechanisms (dynamic clean-room VM analysis, per-publisher trust propagation to dependencies, name-squat prevention, block-list-triggered auto-uninstall) none of which appear in the existing concept.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Official first-party VS Code documentation, directly checkable against the product and Marketplace policy, with a linked Microsoft DevBlogs post giving further detail.

durability.rationale: Describes a stable security architecture (permission model, scanning stack, trust-prompt UX) that has been in place for years, not a version number or pricing detail that will churn.

actionability.rationale: Gives a concrete, checkable set of measures — signature verification, publish-time scanning, verified-publisher badges, block-lists — that directly informs how someone would design or audit an extension distribution channel's trust model.

atomicity.rationale: Every section serves one thesis stated cleanly in a paragraph: because extensions run unsandboxed, the marketplace compensates with layered publish-time, identity, and post-publish controls gated behind per-publisher user consent — a structure comparable to the already-promoted layered-agent-guardrails concept's multiple-mechanisms-under-one-principle shape.
